Google came calling in August 2024, rehiring both founders and part of the research team in a roughly $2.7 billion deal that also licensed Character.AI's technology. Silicon Valley calls this kind of arrangement an acqui-hire, buying the talent without technically buying the company, and Character.AI later largely abandoned building its own large language models, the AI engines that generate the chatbots' text.

Two months after the Google deal, Florida mother Megan Garcia sued Character.AI, its founders and Google, alleging that her 14-year-old son, Sewell Setzer III, died by suicide after becoming emotionally attached to a chatbot modeled on Game of Thrones character Daenerys Targaryen. More lawsuits from other families followed, and in September 2025 the Federal Trade Commission ordered Character.AI and six other tech companies to explain how they protect minors.

A month later, Character.AI banned users under 18 from open-ended chats with its characters, cutting off its core product for its youngest fans. In January, the company and Google agreed to settle lawsuits brought by families in Florida, Colorado, New York, and Texas.

In September 2025, Disney's lawyers sent Character.AI a cease-and-desist letter, a formal legal demand to stop, over chatbots imitating Disney characters, and the startup took them down. This past September, Disney named Character.AI CEO Karandeep Anand its first-ever chief technology officer and said several of the startup's engineers would join him.

Colin Adams, now Character.AI's CEO, said the company spent the past year trying to sustain the business amid "significant legal, regulatory, and operational headwinds" before the board chose a court-supervised sale.

Besides the legal hurdles, the company was burning too much money without reporting enough revenue, reporting “an operating loss of approximately $8-9 million per month.”

Character AI also struggled to raise more capital, which ended up making the whole operation unsustainable. “Notwithstanding the progress that has been made with regulators and personal injury claimants and enhancements to platform safety, Character has faced challenges in obtaining new investment capital,” Character AI CEO Collin Adams said in a sworn statement .

On September 28, Character.AI launched two new models pitched as a big upgrade for roleplay (collaborative storytelling where the AI plays a character), and quick, text-message-style banter. It also rolled out a cheaper subscription called (c.ai) lite, priced at $4.99 a month or $2.49 a week.

Fourteen days later, the company was in bankruptcy court.

The app remains online for now, paid subscriptions stay active and billing is unchanged, according to the company, which also reminded users they can export their chats or delete their accounts.

Character.AI also linked to a support page for anyone struggling with the news, a tacit admission that for some users the app is not just entertainment. AI companions—chatbots designed to act as friends or partners that remember past conversations—can become a daily emotional anchor for people who talk to them for hours.

The page points users to Koko, a nonprofit offering free, anonymous mini-courses of five to 10 minutes on coping with stress and dark thoughts, and to a directory of free helplines staffed by real people. Its very first suggestion, however, is a conversation with a "supportive AI guide," which is to say a chatbot to help people cope with losing their chatbots.

Ledger’s crypto wallet implant scare triggers Trezor reseller crackdown as security fears spread

The rival wallet maker is ending selected retail partnerships despite no confirmed compromise of its devices, while Germany's MediaMarktSaturn suspends Ledger sales.

By Oluwapelumi Adejumo Senior Reporter • CryptoSlate

01 Trezor is cutting authorized resellers after Ledger's hardware implant investigation raised concerns over crypto wallet supply chains. 02 Selected retailers will lose authorization in January 2027, despite Trezor finding no evidence that its own devices were compromised. 03 Ledger is investigating tampering reports in Singapore and Germany, with the source and full extent of the suspected compromise still unknown. Make CryptoSlate preferred on Share

Trezor is cutting authorized resellers after a hardware-implant attack against rival Ledger exposed vulnerabilities in cryptocurrency wallet distribution.

In an Oct. 13 letter , Trezor Chief Commercial Officer Danny Sanders said selected partners would lose their authorization on Jan. 1, 2027, as the company tightens oversight of its supply chain.

The decision marks an escalation in the commercial fallout from the Ledger investigation , which has raised questions about how attackers can introduce malicious components into hardware wallets before they reach customers.

Trezor said it found no evidence of compromised devices within its network, describing the restructuring as a preventive measure.

Trezor sacrifices retail reach for tighter supply-chain controls

Sanders said the company could no longer adequately inspect every partner in its existing distribution network, prompting a review of which retailers should remain authorized. He wrote:

“A hardware wallet is only as safe as the path it travels to reach its owner.”

The company evaluated individual markets based on revenue, distribution coverage, and its ability to reach customers before deciding which partnerships to terminate.

Affected retailers will receive no additional inventory but can continue selling existing stock through the Black Friday and Christmas shopping seasons. Trezor will also remove them from its authorized reseller directory on Jan. 1.

The company did not disclose how many businesses would lose authorization or which markets would be affected.

Sanders acknowledged that the decision could have significant financial consequences for smaller retailers that have built their businesses around Trezor products .

However, he stressed that the restructuring did not reflect wrongdoing by the affected partners or concerns about the safety of their existing inventory. He said:

“This is not a verdict on your business or on the safety of the devices you sell.”

For retailers retaining their authorization, Trezor plans stricter contractual requirements and additional inspections covering how devices are sourced, stored, and handled.

The changes could increase compliance obligations across its remaining distribution network while giving the manufacturer greater control over inventory before it reaches customers.

Related Reading Ledger wallet implant exposes a gap in its authenticity check

Ledger investigation raises questions about authorized retail channels

Trezor's decision follows Ledger's confirmation that attackers installed an unauthorized electronic component inside a wallet sold by CryptoBilis, an official reseller operating in Southeast Asia.

Ledger's Donjon security team found that the implant could capture the 24-word recovery phrase displayed during wallet setup and transmit the information through an LTE connection using an embedded eSIM.

The component operated separately from the device's Secure Element and operating system, allowing attackers to obtain recovery credentials without interfering with normal transaction-signing functions.

Ledger confirmed the discovery on Oct. 10 and said all verified thefts connected to the incident involved devices purchased through CryptoBilis, which has since stopped selling its products.

However, investigators are now examining reports involving additional authorized retailers.

On Oct. 13, Ledger confirmed that MediaMarktSaturn had suspended sales of its hardware wallets across physical stores and online platforms following a report of an implanted device purchased in Germany.

The company said it had not reported any financial losses in connection with the German case.

Separately, former Mt. Gox chief executive Mark Karpelès reported discovering a spying implant inside a Ledger Flex purchased from a MetaPod outlet at Singapore's Changi Airport.

CryptoQuant analyst Darkfost also flagged a reportedly tampered Ledger Flex purchased from Challenger's VivoCity store in Singapore.

Those findings have not been independently confirmed by Ledger or linked to the CryptoBilis attack.

Darkfost subsequently expanded a watchlist of authorized retailers across Southeast Asia and Europe based on potential distribution exposure, while cautioning that inclusion did not establish compromise.

Mapped official resellers across Asia and Europe with potential exposure through infected distribution channels. Source: Darkfost The growing number of reports has intensified scrutiny of where the devices were modified and whether the incidents share a common distribution channel.

Independent blockchain investigators have linked suspected losses approaching $93 million to the broader incident, although Ledger has not verified the total value stolen or the number of affected customers.

The manufacturer maintains that its internal systems and services remain uncompromised.

Ledger's Donjon team is examining additional submitted devices as it works to establish the source and extent of the tampering.

posts.content:
A UK High Court judge has ruled that Chinese law, not English law, must govern the claims of victims to more than 61,000 BTC recovered from a multibillion-pound fraud.

But while the decision settles an important preliminary legal question, it does not determine whether the victims can establish ownership of the cryptocurrency or how much, if anything, they may recover.

This case arises from investment scams arranged by Zhimin Qian in China from 2014 until July 2017. They involved about 10 schemes via the company known as “Tianjin Lantian Gerui Electronic Technology” and others, which included digital currencies, elderly care services, and consumer products. The company lacked authorization to offer financial products and Qian confessed that there was a need for such an authorization under Chinese law.

According to an audit, there were at least 128,409 investment contracts related to the scams; however, as per the court, the number of contracts is not equal to the number of people who were victims of this crime. The total amount of funds collected was approximately 40.23 billion yuan, which is almost £4.1 billion, or over $5 billion.

Most of these funds were used to pay off the previous investors in the schemes whereas some of them were converted into assets, including Bitcoin. More than 100,000 BTC were purchased through a Huobi trading account before Qian left the country in July 2017, crossing into Myanmar to evade arrest.

She arrived in London that September and, together with her associate, Wen, started converting the Bitcoin into other assets. However, she later came under investigation by the Metropolitan Police, who seized four separate devices containing more than 61,000 BTC found in a safety deposit box and a property where the two accomplices were living at the time.

As CryptoPotato reported in October last year, Qian pled guilty at Southwark Crown Court of having possession of criminal property in the form of cryptocurrency. The case established the background to the subsequent dispute over who has the legal right to the recovered assets.

Victims instituted a civil proceeding under Section 281 of the Proceeds of Crime Act 2002, which allows claimants to ask a court to declare the recovered property is theirs, with Justice Turner’s judgement addressing a preliminary question: whether those claims should be assessed under English law, Chinese law, or a combination of both.

According to the judge, Chinese law applies, and he rejected four arguments advanced by applicants seeking to rely on English legal principles. He found that the contracts, investor payments and Bitcoin purchases were rooted in China, and that the location of the cryptocurrency in England did not change which law governed the underlying rights.

Justice Turner also rejected the suggestion that English law should apply by default because the content of Chinese law had not yet been presented in court. As he explained, identifying the applicable law comes before establishing what the law says. The judgement states that applicants’ claimed proprietary rights “must be assessed by reference to Chinese law.”

That distinction matters because Section 281 requires victims to establish an ownership interest in the property, rather than simply show that they lost money in the fraud. The court has not yet determined whether individual applicants have such rights under Chinese law, nor how much they might recover.

Decrypt News Business Binance Is Shutting Down Its Bitcoin Mining Pool After Six Years

Binance will discontinue Binance Pool, Pool Savings, Cloud Mining, and other related services in a retreat from mining infrastructure.

By Jose Antonio Lanz Edited by Guillermo Jimenez

Add on Google Add Decrypt as your preferred source to see more of our stories on Google.

Binance will discontinue Binance Pool, Pool Savings, Cloud Mining, Transaction Accelerator and related features at 07:00 UTC on Nov. 10.

Miners must point their hardware to another pool before the cutoff, and Pool Savings users must redeem their positions before the service ends.

The closure follows Binance's July shutdown of its exchange NFT service and its June push into U.S. stocks and tokenized equities.

Binance will shut down its mining pool and several related services on Nov. 10, the exchange said in an announcement published Tuesday. The closure covers Binance Pool, Pool Savings, Cloud Mining, and Transaction Accelerator, along with Telegram hashrate alerts, email notifications, and the pool's API.

“As part of our ongoing review of products and services, Binance will discontinue Binance Pool and related services on 2026-11-10,” Binance wrote. “All Binance Pool-related services will be discontinued. Binance Pool will begin disconnecting mining connections, and Binance Mining Pool Stratum URLs and mining endpoints will be disabled. Hashrate submissions and mining shares submitted after this time will no longer be accepted, processed, or credited.”

A mining pool combines the computing power of many miners and splits block rewards among them based on the work each one contributes. Cloud Mining let users buy hashrate, a slice of mining power, without owning any hardware, while Transaction Accelerator helped users push through Bitcoin transactions that were slow to confirm because of low fees or network congestion.

Binance pool launched in April 2020 and ranked ninth among Bitcoin pools at the end of 2025, with about 26 exahashes per second, or 2.3% of the network, according to Hashrate Index . One exahash per second equals a quintillion guesses every second at the puzzle that earns a block.

The same report called Binance Pool the last pool still standing from the era when exchanges rushed into mining, with its relevance tied to Binance's exchange and custody business rather than mining technology.

Seems like Binance, just as Satoshi Nakamoto , wants to move onto other things. The shutdown arrives as Binance expands into traditional finance. On June 1, the exchange opened access to more than 7,000 US stocks and ETFs for customers outside the United States, with zero commission and fractional purchases from $5, according to co-CEO Richard Teng. It also previewed bStocks, a coming feature that lets users mint tokenized versions of the shares they buy on the BNB blockchain.

Quantmap co-founder Ivan Patriki told Decrypt at the time that large exchanges are moving into equities because they no longer want to depend on crypto market cycles. Vytautas Mackonis, COO of RWA protocol ALCUM, told Decrypt the offering is more structurally complex than it appears, with Binance as the interface, Nest Trading as the broker-dealer, and Alpaca Securities as the custodian.

Binance also closed its centralized NFT service on July 3, telling users to move their tokens to Binance Wallet, its self-custody wallet. Then-CEO Changpeng Zhao used the phrase “ smooth sunsetting of old products ” in 2023.

At 07:00 UTC on Nov. 10, Binance Pool will begin disconnecting miners and disable its Stratum URLs, the server addresses miners point their machines at to connect to the pool. Shares, the proofs of work that determine each miner's payout, will stop being credited after that time, while those submitted earlier count toward final rewards. Binance said eligible outstanding rewards, balances and refunds will be processed afterward, subject to its product rules, account status and compliance checks.

Decrypt News Business Binance Is Shutting Down Its Bitcoin Mining Pool After Six Years

Binance will discontinue Binance Pool, Pool Savings, Cloud Mining, and other related services in a retreat from mining infrastructure.

By Jose Antonio Lanz Edited by Guillermo Jimenez

Add on Google Add Decrypt as your preferred source to see more of our stories on Google.

Binance will discontinue Binance Pool, Pool Savings, Cloud Mining, Transaction Accelerator and related features at 07:00 UTC on Nov. 10.

Miners must point their hardware to another pool before the cutoff, and Pool Savings users must redeem their positions before the service ends.

The closure follows Binance's July shutdown of its exchange NFT service and its June push into U.S. stocks and tokenized equities.

Binance will shut down its mining pool and several related services on Nov. 10, the exchange said in an announcement published Tuesday. The closure covers Binance Pool, Pool Savings, Cloud Mining, and Transaction Accelerator, along with Telegram hashrate alerts, email notifications, and the pool's API.

“As part of our ongoing review of products and services, Binance will discontinue Binance Pool and related services on 2026-11-10,” Binance wrote. “All Binance Pool-related services will be discontinued. Binance Pool will begin disconnecting mining connections, and Binance Mining Pool Stratum URLs and mining endpoints will be disabled. Hashrate submissions and mining shares submitted after this time will no longer be accepted, processed, or credited.”

A mining pool combines the computing power of many miners and splits block rewards among them based on the work each one contributes. Cloud Mining let users buy hashrate, a slice of mining power, without owning any hardware, while Transaction Accelerator helped users push through Bitcoin transactions that were slow to confirm because of low fees or network congestion.

Binance pool launched in April 2020 and ranked ninth among Bitcoin pools at the end of 2025, with about 26 exahashes per second, or 2.3% of the network, according to Hashrate Index . One exahash per second equals a quintillion guesses every second at the puzzle that earns a block.

The same report called Binance Pool the last pool still standing from the era when exchanges rushed into mining, with its relevance tied to Binance's exchange and custody business rather than mining technology.

Seems like Binance, just as Satoshi Nakamoto , wants to move onto other things. The shutdown arrives as Binance expands into traditional finance. On June 1, the exchange opened access to more than 7,000 US stocks and ETFs for customers outside the United States, with zero commission and fractional purchases from $5, according to co-CEO Richard Teng. It also previewed bStocks, a coming feature that lets users mint tokenized versions of the shares they buy on the BNB blockchain.

Quantmap co-founder Ivan Patriki told Decrypt at the time that large exchanges are moving into equities because they no longer want to depend on crypto market cycles. Vytautas Mackonis, COO of RWA protocol ALCUM, told Decrypt the offering is more structurally complex than it appears, with Binance as the interface, Nest Trading as the broker-dealer, and Alpaca Securities as the custodian.

At 07:00 UTC on Nov. 10, Binance Pool will begin disconnecting miners and disable its Stratum URLs, the server addresses miners point their machines at to connect to the pool. Shares, the proofs of work that determine each miner's payout, will stop being credited after that time, while those submitted earlier count toward final rewards. Binance said eligible outstanding rewards, balances and refunds will be processed afterward, subject to its product rules, account status and compliance checks.

Written by Sam Bourgi staff writer Edited by Robert Lakin staff editor Written by Sam Bourgi staff writer Edited by Robert Lakin staff editor

Most tokenized stock trading on Solana, BNB Chain occurs outside US market hours

Latest News Published Oct 13, 2026 Tokenized equities have reached nearly $3.3 billion in value as investors embrace round-the-clock access beyond Wall Street hours.

Most trading in tokenized stocks on major blockchains now takes place outside regular US market hours, offering an early indication that around-the-clock trading could be one of the biggest advantages of putting equities onchain.

According to Blockworks data cited by The Kobeissi Letter, more than 70% of tokenized stock trading volume on BNB Chain occurs outside the traditional 9:30 am to 4 pm Eastern trading session. The figure is 63% on Solana and nearly 60% on Base.

Meanwhile, Jupiter, a major Solana-based trading platform, reported a 50% month-over-month increase in tokenized asset trading volume.

The figures suggest investors use tokenized stocks to trade when traditional US exchanges are closed, rather than simply replicating activity during regular market hours.

The growth comes as tokenized stock values have increased by 15% over the past 30 days to nearly $3.3 billion, according to RWA.xyz data . A significant portion of that value is concentrated among issuers such as Ondo Global Markets, xStocks and bStocks, whose tokens are issued and traded across different blockchains.

Related: Winners and losers of the SEC’s new tokenized stocks rules

The growth in round-the-clock trading comes as US regulators begin opening the door to tokenized equities in traditional markets. Last month, the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) introduced an “innovation exemption” allowing qualifying venues to trade tokenized US-listed stocks on public blockchains.

SEC Commissioner Mark Uyeda said participating venues must publish transaction data in US dollars, including trade prices, sizes, timestamps and daily trading volumes. They must also disclose liquidity pool addresses and balances.

Unlike existing tokenized stock products such as xStocks and Ondo Global Markets, which are generally unavailable to US investors, the SEC exemption allows qualifying venues to offer tokenized US equities domestically, provided they preserve shareholder rights and meet trading and disclosure requirements.

Decrypt News Coins Bitcoin Whale That Sat Through Every Crash Since 2020 Just Moved $377M

A wallet that received 4,581 BTC in March 2020, worth about $40 million then, moved its stash today when it was worth about $377 million.

By Jose Antonio Lanz Edited by Guillermo Jimenez

Bitcoin whale. Image: Shutterstock/Decrypt

Add on Google Add Decrypt as your preferred source to see more of our stories on Google.

A wallet holding 4,581.94 BTC sent its full balance, worth about $377 million, to five new addresses on Oct. 12 in a single transaction that paid a fee of 732 sats.

The coins arrived in March 2020, when they were worth roughly $40.5 million.

The address received 22 dust deposits since 2020, including 600 sats on Jan. 28, 2025 from a look-alike address matching its first three and last four characters.

A Bitcoin wallet that has held 4,581.94 BTC since March 2020 sent its entire balance to five new addresses on Oct. 12, moving about $377 million in a single transaction, according to blockchain data . The transfer confirmed in block 971,126 at about 18:37 UTC, with Bitcoin trading around $82,350.

Four of the receiving addresses got exactly 1,000 BTC each, and the fifth received 581.94 BTC. The transaction paid a fee of 732 satoshis, the hundred-millionth-of-a-bitcoin units known as sats, or about 60 cents. Bitcoin defies $800 million crypto wipeout as South Korea’s AI stock market crashes

Bitcoin recovers above $83,000 despite a 5.5% plunge in Korean equities, but derivatives data suggest sellers retain control.

By Oluwapelumi Adejumo Senior Reporter • CryptoSlate

01 Bitcoin rebounded above $83,000 despite a sharp Asian stock selloff that sent South Korea's KOSPI down 5.5%. 02 Crypto liquidations reached $813 million, with bullish traders accounting for nearly 85% of the losses. 03 Negative Net Taker Volume raises doubts about Bitcoin's recovery as aggressive sellers retain control. Make CryptoSlate preferred on Share

Bitcoin rebounded above $83,000 on Tuesday despite a sharp Asian stock selloff, as cryptocurrency liquidations exceeded $800 million.

BTC recovered after briefly slipping below $81,000, while semiconductor shares continued a deepening rout that sent South Korea's benchmark KOSPI index down 6%.

South Korea's AI stock collapse exposes concentrated market risks

Reports noted that South Korea's KOSPI plunged up to 7.4% before recovering some losses to close at 6,035.35. The decline briefly pushed the index below 6,000 and triggered a sell-side trading curb as the country's largest semiconductor manufacturers extended their losses.

Samsung Electronics fell 7.39%, while SK Hynix declined 10.09%, marking a fifth consecutive session of losses for both companies.

Together, the two memory-chip manufacturers account for approximately half of the KOSPI's market capitalization, leaving the broader index particularly sensitive to changes in the outlook for AI infrastructure spending.

Foreign investors sold approximately 4.5 trillion won ($3.35 billion) of Korean equities during Tuesday's session, extending a series of withdrawals that have weighed heavily on the country's technology sector.

Investment research firm Paradis Labs said the decline reflected a sustained retreat by foreign institutions from Samsung and SK Hynix.

The firm characterized the prevailing institutional strategy as “Sell Korea, Buy US,” while noting that domestic investors had largely remained patient, with some capital rotating from memory-chip manufacturers into financial stocks.

Paradis Labs also said the deterioration had been building for several sessions, pointing out that recent comments from Broadcom Chief Executive Officer Hock Tan had intensified an existing selloff.

Tan compared speculative AI investment to gambling, adding to concerns that the industry's enormous capital commitments might not generate sufficient returns.

Related Reading Bitcoin’s rebound approaches the $85,000 zone where past buyers may sell

Those remarks coincided with a technological announcement from China's ChangXin Memory Technologies, which said it had developed a DRAM architecture capable of reducing memory-cell area by approximately 30%.

The company plans to introduce products incorporating the technology by the end of 2026, raising concerns about potential competition for South Korean memory producers. Its ability to manufacture the technology commercially at scale remains unproven.

Bitunix analysts said the broader correction reflected growing sensitivity to the financing risks and concentrated investor positioning supporting the AI industry.

The analysts noted that strong semiconductor earnings had not prevented heavy selling, with reduced leveraged exposure and diminished support from share buybacks potentially amplifying the decline.

The pressure has also influenced broader institutional positioning. BlackRock downgraded US equities from overweight to neutral and increased its preference for short-term Treasuries as concerns about AI-related volatility and higher borrowing costs intensified.

Meanwhile, Paradis Labs warned that South Korea's dependence on imported crude oil created another vulnerability as tensions involving Iran escalate . Sustained energy-price increases could compound inflation pressures and weaken confidence in the country's equity market.

The semiconductor weakness has already spread beyond Korea, as the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index declined 2.7% on Monday, while Japan's Nikkei 225 fell 1.8% Tuesday.

Bitcoin's recovery faces pressure after $813 million liquidation wave

Bitcoin's rebound contrasted with sharp losses in Asian equities, but it followed a derivatives market shakeout that wiped out hundreds of millions of dollars in leveraged positions.

According to CoinGlass data, cryptocurrency liquidations reached $812.9 million over 24 hours , affecting 170,209 traders. Bullish positions accounted for $686.72 million, or 84.5% of the total, compared with $126.19 million in bearish bets.

Bitcoin recorded the largest losses at $192.14 million, with long positions accounting for nearly 74% of the total. Ethereum followed with $180.5 million, while Solana saw $60.85 million in liquidations. The largest single liquidation was a $9.65 million Bitcoin long position on Binance .

As Bitcoin declined, forced long-position closures added selling pressure and accelerated the downturn. The subsequent recovery also caught bearish traders off guard, with short liquidations contributing to the sharp reversal.

Yet underlying trading activity suggests that buyers have struggled to regain control despite the price recovery.

CryptoQuant analyst JA Maartunn reported that Bitcoin's Net Taker Volume turned negative again, indicating that aggressive selling in derivatives markets outweighed buying activity.

The reading points to continued selling pressure even as Bitcoin recovers, so passive buying and the closure of bearish positions may be supporting prices without a sustained increase in aggressive demand.

That leaves Bitcoin's recovery exposed to another test if the equity selloff deepens or leveraged traders rebuild positions ahead of Wednesday's US inflation report.

posts.summary: The SHIB Army, the collective term for Shiba Inu holders, supporters, traders, and enthusiasts, has once again found itself in the crosshairs of scammers. Such schemes can lead to painful losses, so here’s how users can protect themselves.
posts.summaryVi: The SHIB Army, the collective term for Shiba Inu holders, supporters, traders, and enthusiasts, has once again found itself in the crosshairs of scammers. Such schemes can lead to painful losses, so here’s how users can protect themselves.
posts.content:
The SHIB Army, the collective term for Shiba Inu holders, supporters, traders, and enthusiasts, has once again found itself in the crosshairs of scammers.

Such schemes can lead to painful losses, so here’s how users can protect themselves.

Recently, an X account falsely claimed a Shiba Inu airdrop was “back,” telling users they were eligible for the dubious campaign after they completed a supposed wallet verification check. The mysterious person or entity also provided a link, but people should not click it, as it was flagged as a scam.

Long-time Shiba Inu community member Marzael.shib warned that no such token distribution exists, calling the development “a drainer.” “They are flooding the timeline; recommend not clicking and report,” they added.

The X account BSCN also sounded the alarm on the matter. The team said the real danger comes when users connect their wallets and sign malicious approvals.

“Those permissions can allow scammers to transfer tokens without stealing a victim’s password,” the warning reads.

The popular meme coin boasts a vast and devoted community, making it a frequent target for scammers. Earlier this year, Shibarium Trustwatch (an X account dedicated to warning Shiba Inu users about potential threats) warned about numerous fraud attempts involving the SOU NFT.

Its team clarified that users will never receive the non-fungible token in question, and that eligible users can claim it only through Shiba Inu’s official website.

“Do not click on shared, shortened, or copied links. Scammers often create fake websites that look identical to the real one in order to steal funds. Always type the official address directly into your browser and verify you are on the correct domain before connecting your wallet. Never share your private keys or seed phrase with anyone under any circumstances,” it added.

Prior to that, the same X account warned that bad actors created a malicious website impersonating Shiba Inu’s official platform. The fake site includes “special” promotions and false claims of collaborations and presale bonuses, designed to lure people into connecting their wallets.

The meme coin’s price has plunged by nearly 12% over the past week. However, the main reason for the drop appears to be the overall decline in the cryptocurrency market during that period, not the scam warning that could have spread panic across the community.

As of this writing, SHIB trades around $0.000005163 (per CoinGecko), down 95% from its late-2021 all-time high. Analysts have been relatively silent on the token lately, yet certain technical indicators may help traders identify the next potential move.

Today (October 13), Shiba Inu coins stored on crypto exchanges fell to a near one-month low of roughly 87.2 trillion. This can be interpreted as a bullish signal since it reduces immediate selling pressure.

posts.content:
1.13% TRX $0.3275 0.65% LINK $12.93 0.79% ZEC $1,224.04 2.01% ADA $0.2369 0.24% XRP $1.37 1.50% ETH $2,513.45 1.26% BTC $83,494.26 1.27% XMR $545.20 2.29% BNB $743.18 0.30% XLM $0.1911 1.37% SOL $106.94 0.25% HYPE $81.87 0.77%

Written by Turner Wright staff writer Edited by Sam Bourgi staff writer Written by Turner Wright staff writer Edited by Sam Bourgi staff writer

Trezor reduces resellers as a ‘preventative step’ amid Ledger tampering reports

Latest News Published Oct 13, 2026 CCO Danny Sanders said he had notified certain hardware wallet resellers that they would be removed from Trezor’s list of authorized entities starting Jan. 1.

Hardware wallet producer Trezor announced it would reduce its number of resellers as a “preventive step, taken out of an abundance of caution,” following reports that malicious implants had been installed in devices made by competitor Ledger.

In a Tuesday X post, Trezor said there was “not a single piece of evidence that [its] devices have been compromised” after reports that Ledger hardware wallet users had found malicious implants that exposed recovery phrases.

However, Trezor said that it would reduce the number of its resellers, citing “recent supply-chain incidents.” Chief commercial officer Danny Sanders added that he had notified certain resellers that they would be removed from the company’s list of authorized entities on Jan. 1, and would halt shipments of Trezor devices starting on Tuesday.

Trezor’s response came just days after Ledger confirmed that at least one of its devices purchased by a Southeast Asian reseller contained an unauthorized hardware implant, potentially leading to millions of dollars in losses for users. The wallets, sold by reseller CryptoBilis, captured recovery phrases and transmitted them over cellular networks.

“Our setup checks are built to catch counterfeit devices and modified firmware,” a Trezor spokesperson told Cointelegraph. “The implant found in a device bought from CryptoBilis works differently. This is a unique way of tampering with the device, which doesn’t modify the firmware, but reads information on the screen and later sends it to the attacker. So far, we have not seen this specific type of attack on Trezor devices in the real world.”

Related: Ledger investigates fund losses linked to Southeast Asian reseller, warns users

During the investigation, CryptoBilis, an authorized Trezor reseller, suspended all hardware wallet sales. The parent company of European electronics retailer MediaMarkt also announced that it had removed all Ledger products from its physical stores and online platforms “as a precautionary measure.”

Blockchain sleuths are still investigating the extent of losses for hardware wallet users, but research from two individuals suggested between $72 million and $86 million. Ledger reported on Tuesday that it had “not confirmed the total number of affected users or the total value lost” due to the breaches.

The Trezor spokesperson advised users to buy products directly from the company, “checking the seal is intact,” and consider a multisignature wallet “with devices from different makers, so one compromised device can’t move funds on its own.”

posts.content:
Ethereum Name Service plans major .eth overhaul with one irreversible catch for domain holders

ENSv2 would allow users to keep their existing domains, but those who migrate cannot return to the old system.

By Oluwapelumi Adejumo Senior Reporter • CryptoSlate

01 Ethereum Name Service has proposed activating ENSv2, allowing .eth holders to migrate permanently or remain on the existing system. 02 The upgrade would raise annual fees for longer domain names by 60% while introducing stablecoin payments and flexible domain management. 03 The DAO has yet to approve activation, leaving the launch date and potential disruptions during the transition unresolved. Make CryptoSlate preferred on Share

Ethereum Name Service has proposed activating ENSv2 without requiring existing .eth domain holders to migrate to the new system.

The Oct. 11 proposal would let users keep their current names indefinitely, as long as they keep renewing them, while offering a permanent migration option for those who want access to upgraded features.

Once activated, ENSv2 would handle all new .eth registrations, replacing the existing registration infrastructure. Holders who migrate would permanently transfer management of their domains to the new system, with no mechanism for returning their original tokens.

The proposal remains subject to approval by the ENS decentralized autonomous organization (DAO), whose Oct. 12 governance bulletin listed the vote as pending. ENS has not announced a launch date.

ENSv2 introduces permanent migration and higher registration fees

The upgrade would replace ENS's existing registry, introduced in 2017, with a hierarchical structure that allows individual domains to maintain separate registries for their subdomains.

The changes would give owners more flexibility in assigning permissions, letting businesses and decentralized applications delegate responsibility for specific names or records without giving up broader control.

During the migration, an owner's existing ENSv1 token would move into a smart contract known as the Graveyard, which cannot return or transfer the tokens it receives.

However, users who choose to remain on ENSv1 would keep access to their domains and continue renewing them through a dedicated contract that also preserves their ENSv2 reservations.

The transition would introduce changes to registration costs.

Thanks for signing up to The Catalyst. Look out for your first daily email. If you already receive it, you’re all set.

According to ENS's official guidance , annual fees for names containing five or more characters would rise 60% to $8 from $5, while prices for three- and four-character names would remain unchanged.

ENSv2 would also introduce discounts for longer registrations, reducing annual costs by approximately 44% for users purchasing six or more years.

Registration and renewal payments would use stablecoins, including USDC and DAI, replacing ETH -denominated payments and keeping fees fixed in dollar terms.

Domain expiration rules would also change.

The existing 90-day grace period would shrink to 28 days for migrated names. To compensate, ENS would extend registration expiry dates by 62 days, preserving the original deadline when names become available to others.

Names remaining on ENSv1 would retain their 90-day grace period, while domains already expired beyond that window would not receive reservations in the new registry.

The activation process presents additional operational challenges.

ENS expects to temporarily suspend new registrations while developers synchronize existing records and activate the new infrastructure, a process expected to take several hours.

The proposal includes conflicting provisions on renewals during that interval, leaving uncertainty about whether existing holders can renew names before ENSv2 becomes operational.

Related Reading DAOs are forcing crypto protocols to choose between code and emergency brakes

Wallets and applications integrating ENS must also update their resolution infrastructure to support the new system.

Following approval, ENS Labs would complete the final synchronization, activate ENSv2 registration and resolution, and transfer its remaining administrative permissions to the DAO.

The timing of those steps, along with clarification on renewal availability during the transition, remains unresolved ahead of the governance vote.

Strive Asset Management at the New York Stock Exchange. Image: Decrypt/NYSE Group

Strive bought 3,311 BTC worth roughly $280 million between Oct. 5 and Oct. 9 at an average price of about $84,500 per coin, its largest purchase since January, lifting holdings to 32,773 BTC.

The buy caps an aggressive run—following $169 million and $94.5 million purchases—for the firm, which trades as ASST and recently merged with Semler Scientific to grow its balance sheet.

It lands amid heavy treasury activity from Strategy, Solana’s DeFi Dev Corp. and Bitmine, as Strive bought into a dip well below Bitcoin’s recent highs.

Strive is piling into Bitcoin at its fastest clip of the year, scooping up another 3,311 BTC worth roughly $280 million in its biggest single purchase since January.

The Nasdaq-listed asset manager, which trades under the ticker ASST, disclosed in a filing Monday that it bought the Bitcoin between Oct. 5 and Oct. 9 at an average price of about $84,500 per coin, including fees. The buy lifts Strive’s total holdings to 32,773 BTC, worth roughly $2.73 billion at today’s prices, up from 29,462 BTC a week earlier.

The purchase caps a stretch of aggressive accumulation. Strive added $169 million in Bitcoin earlier this month in what was then its largest buy in four months, after pushing its stack past 27,000 BTC with a $94.5 million purchase in late September.

The latest tranche extends that momentum, and the timing is notable: the firm bought as Bitcoin slid through a rough week, picking up coins at an average price well below the token’s recent highs near $87,000.

Strive, led by CEO Matthew Cole, is among a wave of public companies that have adopted Bitcoin treasury strategies, raising capital to stockpile the asset and tie their share price to its performance.

Beyond its Bitcoin, the company also holds about 505,000 shares of Strategy’s STRC preferred stock, valued near $50 million, and roughly $310 million in cash.

The buying spree arrives amid a flurry of treasury activity across the sector. Strategy itself recently added $21.5 million in Bitcoin while buying back preferred stock, Solana treasury firm DeFi Development Corp. kept accumulating SOL , and Bitmine continued stacking Ethereum , though chairman Tom Lee said that company is nearly finished and will halt purchases once it holds 5% of the token’s supply.

The strategy carries the category’s familiar risk: Strive’s fortunes rise and fall with a notoriously volatile asset. Buying into a dip can pay off if Bitcoin rebounds, but the same exposure cuts the other way, and treasury firms have faced scrutiny over how much their stock premiums depend on continued accumulation.

Decrypt News Artificial Intelligence AI Researchers Are Smoking Cigarettes to Prove AI Will Cure Cancer, Says Palantir Exec

Palantir CTO Shyam Sankar says many AI researchers have taken up smoking to signal their faith in AI.

By Jose Antonio Lanz Edited by Guillermo Jimenez

Smoke 'em if you got 'em. Image: Unsplash

Add on Google Add Decrypt as your preferred source to see more of our stories on Google.

Palantir CTO Shyam Sankar claimed on CBS that many AI researchers have started smoking to show how much they believe in AI.

Sankar provide any data, and used the segment to attack effective altruism as a doomsday cult.

The CDC says smoking causes about one in three U.S. cancer deaths, and Anthropic's Dario Amodei says only actually curing cancer will earn public trust in AI.

Nothing says "I trust the future of medicine" quite like lighting a Marlboro and waiting for the chatbot to fix your lungs. That is the habit Palantir CTO Shyam Sankar says is spreading among AI researchers, who have supposedly started smoking cigarettes to prove how confident they are that AI will cure cancer.

"So many AI researchers have started smoking as a way of signaling to other researchers how much they believe in AI," Sankar said in an interview on CBS News' " Face the Nation " on Sunday. "I believe so much in AI that it's going to cure cancer. So I'm showing you my chips are all in."

He did not name a single researcher, cite a survey, or explain how he knows. The remark landed as an aside while host Margaret Brennan pressed him on why he was so focused on the topic.

He pointed to FTX founder Sam Bankman-Fried as the effective altruist most Americans know, calling the movement a "millenarian doomsday cult." He also invoked Pascal's idea of a god-shaped hole in every human heart, which he suggested some of these researchers are filling with a machine god called AGI.

The medical record is less enthusiastic than the thesis. The CDC says smoking causes roughly one in three cancer deaths in the United States, and cigarette smoke contains at least 69 chemicals known to cause cancer.

Smokers face about 25 times the lung cancer risk of non-smokers, according to the agency. Quitting lowers the risk of 12 types of cancer, and the added lung cancer risk drops by half 10 to 15 years after stopping.

The cancer pitch is not new in this industry. Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei said in August that promising AI will cure cancer has become “more a cliche than it is inspiring,” and that only actually curing it would earn the public's trust.

2/2 Second, on the messaging around AI. I do not agree that my messaging has been disproportionately negative. In fact it has been about equally balanced between risks and benefits: I’ve written one major essay about each, and even in interviews where I discuss the risks, I…

— Dario Amodei (@DarioAmodei) August 15, 2026

That trust is thin. In the CBS poll Brennan cited, 50% of Americans said AI will create more problems than it solves, 29% said it will solve more than it creates, and 21% were unsure.

About 45% said they want the government to restrict AI's use and development. Smoking to show faith in the technology does not obviously help that number, but it does help AI bros bond with each other. "When you're smoking, you're networking by accident," Revamp AI cofounder Stephen Campbell told Business Insider last month.

The IMF's Kristalina Georgieva recently warned that AI could hit 40% of jobs , and insiders expect a major AI incident within a year. Indirectly causing a lung cancer outbreak was probably not on their bingo card.

Palantir sells data-analysis software to governments and militaries. Most of its business relies on AI.

posts.content:
Blur will shut down its frontend on November 12, 2026. But the NFT marketplace won’t disappear. Its protocol will keep running on-chain, and the BLUR token will still control the fee switch.

The same date also marks a change for Blend, Blur’s lending platform. It will stop matching new loans, giving borrowers until then to repay or risk default. Users who still have assets on Blend will get a withdrawal tool after the deadline, according to the announcement.

Blur raised $11 million in seed funding in March 2022 and emerged as a major rival to OpenSea, targeting professional NFT traders. After launching in October, it attracted users with zero marketplace fees, bulk trading tools, and token rewards. Its BLUR token launch in February 2023 brought a wave of activity, while Blend later expanded Blur into NFT-backed lending. By December 2023, it commanded 80% of the NFT market’s share .

Blur still maintained its lead in Q1 2024 after recording $1.5 billion in volume. However, falling NFT activity and declining lending demand gradually weakened its position. By 2025, OpenSea was recovering market share, while Blend went in the opposite direction. In April 2026, KuCoin removed BLUR cross-margin trading. Two months later, Binance placed the token under its “Monitoring Tag.”

2026 has seen several crypto and Web3 platforms announce shutdowns or wind-downs. NFT platform Nifty Gateway and social collecting app Rodeo announced plans to wind down, while Foundation announced its closure in April after a sale fell through. Meanwhile, Blur’s news comes less than a fortnight after Blast announced it would close on October 2.

Interestingly, both projects were created by Blur founder Tieshun Roquerre, better known as Pacman, and developed by the same team. Blast, an Ethereum scaling network, also revealed it was ceasing operations just over two years after launch. It said that “the economics of operating the chain no longer make sense.” Activity on the network had faded, which left it unable to cover its running costs.

Chayanika has been working as a financial journalist for seven years. A graduate in Political Science and Journalism, her interest lies in regulatory implications with a focus on technological evolution in the crypto realm.

News Australia Image by CryptoSlate Derivatives

Australia moves to close crypto derivatives loophole after retail traders lose A$458 million

ASIC wants to extend existing trading safeguards to qualifying crypto-settled derivatives as losses mount across the broader CFD market.

By Oluwapelumi Adejumo Senior Reporter • CryptoSlate

01 Australia plans to extend retail trading protections to qualifying crypto-settled derivatives, closing a regulatory gap in existing CFD rules. 02 ASIC's proposal follows A$458 million in retail CFD losses, with 68% of clients losing money during the 2023–24 financial year. 03 Brokers face potential changes to leverage and margin requirements, with industry feedback due by Nov. 9. Make CryptoSlate preferred on Share

Australia's markets regulator proposed extending retail leverage restrictions to crypto-settled derivatives amid mounting losses among investors trading risky financial products.

On Oct. 12, the Australian Securities and Investments Commission (ASIC) announced it wants to expand its existing contracts-for-difference (CFD) rules to cover qualifying derivatives settled through digital assets, closing a regulatory gap that lets economically similar products face different restrictions.

The proposal follows ASIC's finding that 68% of retail CFD clients lost money during the 2023–24 financial year, with combined losses exceeding A$458 million ($325 million), including A$73 million in fees. The figures cover CFD trading across asset classes, rather than cryptocurrency derivatives alone.

The Australian regulator is also seeking to extend its existing investor protections for another decade, keeping them in force until 2037, subject to government approval.

Australia targets leveraged crypto products and margin practices

Under ASIC's existing framework, CFDs are generally covered when transactions are settled in cash or through offsetting obligations between counterparties.

However, some derivatives with similar characteristics can settle through transfers of digital assets, potentially placing them outside the current product intervention order.

ASIC wants to eliminate that distinction by extending the definition to qualifying digitally settled contracts, regardless of whether their underlying exposure is linked to cryptocurrencies, traditional assets, interest rates or market indices.

The change could force affected brokers and derivatives platforms to comply with existing leverage restrictions, standardized margin close-out arrangements, negative balance protections and limits on promotional incentives.

For CFDs referencing cryptocurrencies, the current maximum retail leverage is 2:1, meaning investors must provide at least half the value of their positions as initial margin.

Other contracts face different limits depending on the underlying asset, ranging from 5:1 for shares to 30:1 for major currency pairs.

The proposed expansion would therefore depend on a derivative's underlying exposure and contractual structure, rather than automatically imposing the cryptocurrency leverage cap on every product settled using digital assets.

Some fixed-expiry crypto futures and options would remain outside the framework.

ASIC Commissioner Alan Kirkland said existing restrictions had materially reduced investor harm, particularly by limiting excessive leverage.

Thanks for signing up to The Catalyst. Look out for your first daily email. If you already receive it, you’re all set.

During the first six months after the protections took effect in March 2021, aggregate quarterly retail losses declined 91%, from A$372 million to A$33 million.

The regulator also recorded an 87% reduction in quarterly margin close-outs, although subsequent reviews showed that most retail CFD investors continued losing money.

ASIC's latest proposal would tighten how brokers calculate initial margin, following a sector-wide investigation that identified firms offsetting customers' opposing trading positions to reduce collateral requirements.

Under the proposed clarification, brokers must calculate the minimum margin separately for each CFD, preventing them from using one position to reduce the initial collateral required for another.

The regulator said its intervention over margin-netting practices led 28 issuers to refund more than A$36 million to affected retail customers.

Additional changes target CFDs linked to options, where investor losses have been particularly severe.

ASIC found that 85% of retail clients trading CFDs over options lost money during 2023–24, prompting proposals to clarify margin requirements and examine whether some products should remain available to ordinary investors.

The regulator is specifically seeking evidence on contracts that could expose traders to losses exceeding the options premium, including structures with potentially unlimited downside exposure.

It has yet to decide whether those products should face further restrictions or an outright prohibition.

Australia's ASIC also wants tighter conditions for promotional discounts, requiring permitted offers to be available on substantially equal terms to retail customers and prominently displayed on brokers' websites and trading platforms.

Related Reading Australia gives crypto firms until Sept. 30 to get licensed or risk enforcement

The proposals would require firms to retain records of qualifying discounts for seven years after the offers end, while ensuring educational and research tools are not used to encourage prohibited trading activity.

The existing CFD intervention order expires on May 23, 2027. ASIC argues that a further 10-year extension would give firms greater regulatory certainty while preserving the regulator's ability to revoke the restrictions earlier.

However, the amendments remain under consultation, and industry feedback could change their final scope.

ASIC is seeking submissions from brokers, trading platforms and consumer groups by Nov. 9, including information about which digitally settled products would be affected, expected compliance costs and whether firms would need a transition period.

Written by Turner Wright staff writer Edited by Robert Lakin staff editor Written by Turner Wright staff writer Edited by Robert Lakin staff editor

How the SEC’s lack of leadership could facilitate crypto rulemaking

Latest News Published Oct 13, 2026 A recent change in the SEC’s rules on quorum could make it easier for the agency to amend its approach to crypto regulation in the absence of a market structure bill.

After US lawmakers failed to pass a comprehensive digital asset market structure bill, financial regulators stepped up efforts to change rules around the oversight and enforcement of crypto companies and offerings.

However, the two primary regulators, the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) and Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC), are understaffed at the leadership level, leaving the decisions for regulating aspects of the $3 trillion crypto market largely in the hands of just three individuals, two of whom were nominated by US President Donald Trump.

At the SEC, two commissioners — Chair Paul Atkins and former Acting Chair Mark Uyeda — remain following the departure of Commissioner Hester Peirce earlier this month. The dearth of leadership at the CFTC is even more stark, with Michael Selig serving as the only Senate-confirmed chair and commissioner since December 2025. The agencies are intended to each have five commissioners.

Both agencies have proposed rules that appear to be attempting to take the place of legislation from Congress in regulating cryptocurrencies.

The SEC proposed rules to provide companies with a safe harbor from tokens being treated as “investment contracts” in August, and the CFTC followed suit in October, with Selig saying the agency would use its “existing statutory authorities“ to address crypto regulation through proposed rules on exchanges. Atkins added on Oct. 2 that “more regulatory proposals [were] on the horizon” for crypto.

On Sept. 30, the SEC made these regulatory avenues even easier with a lack of commissioners. The agency released a final rule which went into effect on Oct. 2 that it said amended quorum requirements for what it called “promot[ing] flexibility and finality of agency rulemaking.” The rule reduces the number of commissioners required for a quorum to just one person if only two are present in many cases.

“[...] with now just two commissioners around and it being entirely possible that one of them might have to recuse themselves from an issue (or be otherwise MIA), just one is now enough to pass a formal rule that applies to America’s vast multitrillion-dollar securities markets,” wrote Robin Wigglesworth in an Oct. 5 op-ed for the Financial Times.

Related: Crypto regulation at SEC, CFTC to come down to 3 commissioners following key resignation

Uyeda responded in his own Financial Times op-ed on Sunday, claiming that the SEC’s “commitment to its mission remains unchanged” despite having only two commissioners and no announcement from Trump about additional nominations to fill the empty seats. The policymaker said that the rule change “clarifies that the Commission can establish a quorum if all but one commissioner is disqualified from a matter.”

“Suggesting that the SEC is ‘hastily revamp[ing]’ its quorum rule so that the remaining commissioners can ‘have their way’ makes for a colourful comparison to fictional dystopian regimes but misleads readers about why the Commission revised its quorum rule and why it’s for the better,” said Uyeda.

As of Tuesday, the White House had not announced any nominations for the SEC and CFTC, potentially leaving the rulemaking process in the hands of just one person at each agency for months, if not longer. Congress still has time to vote on the market structure bill at the center of the controversy, the Digital Asset Market Clarity (CLARITY) Act, but some experts don’t see lawmakers advancing the legislation in a lame duck session between the 2026 midterm elections and when the next session is sworn into office in January.

posts.summaryVi: The November 2024 election, which saw Donald Trump become America’s 47th president, triggered a major cryptocurrency rally.
posts.content:
The November 2024 election, which saw Donald Trump become America’s 47th president, triggered a major cryptocurrency rally. After all, the Republican presented himself as a strong supporter of the industry throughout his campaign, promising to make the USA a global crypto hub, promote innovation, establish a strategic Bitcoin reserve, ban the creation of a CBDC, and implement a more favorable regulatory framework for digital assets.

During his nearly two years in office, he fulfilled several promises, but other decisions have increased geopolitical tensions and negatively affected financial and crypto markets. With that in mind, we asked three of the most widely used AI-powered chatbots to assess how Bitcoin might react if the Republicans lose the midterms next month. Here’s what they had to say.

Meanwhile, the chatbot warned that a collapse is not completely out of the question and may occur only if election results align with falling ETF inflows, higher interest rates from the Federal Reserve, or a major deleveraging event.

“However, unless accompanied by a major macroeconomic shock (like hawkish Federal Reserve pivots or liquidity contractions), such a pullback would represent a temporary price adjustment rather than a fundamental trend reversal,” it added.

At the same time, Martinez doesn’t think this could stop BTC’s overall bullish move, viewing a potential drop after the elections as a perfect buying opportunity.

Decrypt News Business Trezor Cuts Its Resellers After Ledger Finds Spy Implant in Crypto Wallets

Trezor is ending reseller authorizations on January 1, 2027, after Ledger confirmed that wallets sold by a Southeast Asian retailer carried a hidden implant that sent out users' recovery phrases.

By Jose Antonio Lanz Edited by Guillermo Jimenez

Add on Google Add Decrypt as your preferred source to see more of our stories on Google.

Trezor told partners their reseller authorization ends January 1, 2027, and that it will ship them no new stock, saying there is no evidence its devices were compromised.

Ledger's Donjon team says wallets sold by Southeast Asian reseller CryptoBilis held an implant that captures recovery phrases from the screen and sends them over LTE.

Onchain investigator Specter traced more than $86 million in suspected thefts, a figure Ledger says it has not verified.

Trezor is cutting its network of authorized resellers, telling partners their authorization ends on January 1, 2027, days after rival hardware wallet manufacturer Ledger started an investigation that eventually confirmed a hidden spy implant in crypto wallets sold through a third-party store.

The company announced the move on X on Tuesday, saying “there is not a single piece of evidence” that Trezor devices have been compromised. It described the cut as a preventive step taken out of caution.

“Following recent supply-chain incidents, we decided to reduce the number of resellers so we can more effectively check those we work with,” Trezor wrote.

A hardware wallet is a small device that keeps the secret keys to your crypto offline, away from hackers. Setting one up produces a 24-word recovery phrase that works as a master password: whoever has those words can empty the wallet from anywhere in the world.

Ledger's Donjon security team says wallets sold by CryptoBilis, a reseller in Southeast Asia, contained an unauthorized component that reads the screen and decodes the recovery phrase when it appears. The spy implant then sends the words out over LTE, the same mobile data network your phone uses, through an eSIM, a SIM card built into the hardware. Ledger says the implant does not alter the chip that stores the keys or the device's operating system, so a tampered wallet looks and works normally.

Trezor CCO Danny Sanders shared the letter that the company sent to those providers that Trezor is ditching. “If you are receiving this letter, your authorization ends on 1 January 2027. On that date we will remove you from our list of authorized Trezor resellers,” the letter reads. “I am sorry. This decision says nothing about your effort or the way you represented us.”

This is a precautionary measure to protect our supply chain and our customers,” he wrote. “If things change in the future we will review it.”

Affected resellers will get no new stock, but they can keep selling what they have through Black Friday and the holiday season. Sanders said the decision just reflects how many partners Trezor can vet closely itself.

Neither the post nor the letter says how many resellers are affected. Trezor says it reviewed each country on its own, weighing revenue and distribution against its own presence there, and that resellers who stay will face an updated legal framework and tighter rules on how devices are sourced, stored, and handled.

Trezor said on X earlier this week that CryptoBilis was already off its seller list and that it had received no reports of tampered Trezors from the retailer.

Hi, don’t open it. Forcing the casing open can damage the device, and if it’s a Safe 7, the built-in battery makes that genuinely risky. If something about your device worries you, reach out via https://t.co/wzwW038oLv , and we’ll take a look.

In May 2022, Trezor warned that counterfeit Model T wallets were being sold on a Russian marketplace by a seller that was not an authorized reseller. The devices had been opened, resealed, and fitted with replaced internal components, and Trezor said the recovery phrases they generated were predictable or predefined, meaning someone else could already know the words.

Trezor's advice then was to buy only from its official shop or an authorized reseller. The second option is the network it is now shrinking.

In August, shipping partner ShipMonk exposed Trezor customer data after unauthorized access, and Trezor's September update put the total at 80,689 customers . Trezor says its systems, devices, private keys, and wallet backups were not affected.

Ledger told anyone who bought from CryptoBilis in the past 90 days not to set up their device, and told those who already did to move their funds to a new seed phrase on a device bought from Ledger. Ledger and Trezor have each warned buyers against unauthorized sellers.

Decrypt News Business Trezor Cuts Its Resellers After Ledger Finds Spy Implant in Crypto Wallets

Trezor is ending reseller authorizations on January 1, 2027, after Ledger confirmed that wallets sold by a Southeast Asian retailer carried a hidden implant that sent out users' recovery phrases.

By Jose Antonio Lanz Edited by Guillermo Jimenez

Add on Google Add Decrypt as your preferred source to see more of our stories on Google.

Trezor told partners their reseller authorization ends January 1, 2027, and that it will ship them no new stock, saying there is no evidence its devices were compromised.

Ledger's Donjon team says wallets sold by Southeast Asian reseller CryptoBilis held an implant that captures recovery phrases from the screen and sends them over LTE.

Onchain investigator Specter traced more than $86 million in suspected thefts, a figure Ledger says it has not verified.

Trezor is cutting its network of authorized resellers, telling partners their authorization ends on January 1, 2027, days after rival hardware wallet manufacturer Ledger started an investigation that eventually confirmed a hidden spy implant in crypto wallets sold through a third-party store.

The company announced the move on X on Tuesday, saying “there is not a single piece of evidence” that Trezor devices have been compromised. It described the cut as a preventive step taken out of caution.

“Following recent supply-chain incidents, we decided to reduce the number of resellers so we can more effectively check those we work with,” Trezor wrote.

A hardware wallet is a small device that keeps the secret keys to your crypto offline, away from hackers. Setting one up produces a 24-word recovery phrase that works as a master password: whoever has those words can empty the wallet from anywhere in the world.

Ledger's Donjon security team says wallets sold by CryptoBilis, a reseller in Southeast Asia, contained an unauthorized component that reads the screen and decodes the recovery phrase when it appears. The spy implant then sends the words out over LTE, the same mobile data network your phone uses, through an eSIM, a SIM card built into the hardware. Ledger says the implant does not alter the chip that stores the keys or the device's operating system, so a tampered wallet looks and works normally.

Trezor CCO Danny Sanders shared the letter that the company sent to those providers that Trezor is ditching. “If you are receiving this letter, your authorization ends on 1 January 2027. On that date we will remove you from our list of authorized Trezor resellers,” the letter reads. “I am sorry. This decision says nothing about your effort or the way you represented us.”

This is a precautionary measure to protect our supply chain and our customers,” he wrote. “If things change in the future we will review it.”

Affected resellers will get no new stock, but they can keep selling what they have through Black Friday and the holiday season. Sanders said the decision just reflects how many partners Trezor can vet closely itself.

Neither the post nor the letter says how many resellers are affected. Trezor says it reviewed each country on its own, weighing revenue and distribution against its own presence there, and that resellers who stay will face an updated legal framework and tighter rules on how devices are sourced, stored, and handled.

Trezor said on X earlier this week that CryptoBilis was already off its seller list and that it had received no reports of tampered Trezors from the retailer.

Hi, don’t open it. Forcing the casing open can damage the device, and if it’s a Safe 7, the built-in battery makes that genuinely risky. If something about your device worries you, reach out via https://t.co/wzwW038oLv , and we’ll take a look.

In May 2022, Trezor warned that counterfeit Model T wallets were being sold on a Russian marketplace by a seller that was not an authorized reseller. The devices had been opened, resealed, and fitted with replaced internal components, and Trezor said the recovery phrases they generated were predictable or predefined, meaning someone else could already know the words.

Trezor's advice then was to buy only from its official shop or an authorized reseller. The second option is the network it is now shrinking.

In August, shipping partner ShipMonk exposed Trezor customer data after unauthorized access, and Trezor's September update put the total at 80,689 customers . Trezor says its systems, devices, private keys, and wallet backups were not affected.

Ledger told anyone who bought from CryptoBilis in the past 90 days not to set up their device, and told those who already did to move their funds to a new seed phrase on a device bought from Ledger. Ledger and Trezor have each warned buyers against unauthorized sellers.

Strive reports $208M in warrant exercises as Bitcoin holdings jump 11%

Latest News Published Oct 13, 2026 Strive is now the fifth-largest publicly traded corporate Bitcoin holder, with 32,773 BTC, as it continues to expand its treasury through equity financing.

Strive, a publicly traded Bitcoin treasury company, increased its holdings by more than 11% last week as investors exercised $208 million in warrants, with Bitcoin purchases outpacing share issuance and giving existing shareholders greater exposure to the cryptocurrency.

In a Tuesday filing with the US Securities and Exchange Commission, Strive disclosed that it purchased 3,311 Bitcoin (BTC) in the week ending Oct. 9 at an average price of approximately $84,500 per coin. The purchases brought its total holdings to 32,773 BTC, making it the fifth-largest publicly traded corporate Bitcoin holder, according to industry data .

At last look on Tuesday, Bitcoin was trading hands at roughly $83,300 apiece, according to Yahoo Finance data. The Strive (ASST) share price was little changed at $27.52.

Strive Chairman and CEO Matt Cole said on X that investors had exercised $208 million in warrants, with approximately 15.3 million remaining ahead of their Tuesday expiration.

The company also amended its governing documents to set a binding $100 minimum issuance price for its SATA preferred shares, limiting its ability to issue them below that threshold. Those shares were trading at $99.40, at last look.

Strive’s latest purchases increased its Bitcoin holdings per share even as the company issued additional equity. During the reporting period, its Bitcoin reserves grew 11.2%, outpacing a 9.4% increase in its effective common share count.

Related: Treasury yields at 5% threaten extending Bitcoin’s best quarter since 2017

Strive’s latest purchase drew praise from Michael Saylor, whose company, Strategy, pioneered the corporate Bitcoin treasury model.

“Strive is turning demand for digital equity (ASST) and digital credit (SATA) into demand for Bitcoin,” Saylor wrote on X. “Its hypergrowth shows how the capital markets are accelerating Bitcoin adoption.”

Saylor was referring to Strive’s use of common and preferred shares to raise capital for Bitcoin purchases, a strategy similar to Strategy’s own approach through its MSTR common stock and STRC preferred shares.

Strategy added a comparatively modest 250 BTC to its treasury last week, bringing its total holdings to 848,250 BTC and maintaining its position as the largest publicly traded corporate Bitcoin holder.

Related: Saylor teases Strategy Bitcoin buying after ending September with STRC buybacks

Finance Crypto exchange MNX takes on OKX, Bitget offering pre-IPO futures for AI giants

MNX is offering a different way to trade the future valuations of private AI companies, including OpenAI, Anthropic and DeepSeek.

By Olivier Acuna | Edited by Jamie Crawley Updated Oct 13, 2026, 2:07 p.m. EDT Published Oct 13, 2026, 11:52 a.m. EDT

2 min read Make preferred on Share 

AI is driving one of the largest investment cycles in history, said MXN investor, Max Killberg of Village Global. (Growtika/Unsplash) Summary Show MNX, is a new crypto exchange that offers futures contracts that let investors speculate on the valuations of private artificial intelligence companies including OpenAI, Anthropic, DeepSeek and Moonshot. Unlike competing perpetual futures, MNX’s contracts expire at the end of 2027 and carry no recurring funding fees, but their settlement prices may differ from the prices investors would pay for private shares. The exchange allows traders to use up to three times their available funds, does not currently serve U.S. customers and plans to expand into markets tied to the broader A.I. economy.

A new cryptocurrency exchange will allow investors to speculate on the valuations of private artificial intelligence (AI) giants like OpenAI and Anthropic when they go public.

MNX, a new crypto exchange developed by former Manifold executives, went live on Tuesday offering futures contracts tied to OpenAI, Anthropic, DeepSeek and Moonshot. The platform, built on MegaETH blockchain, raised $6.4 million from investors led by Village Global in June.

Larger crypto exchanges, including OKX and Bitget, already offer contracts that let traders bet on the value of private AI companies without owning their shares.

Unlike Bitget’s perpetual futures which never expire, MNX offers contracts with expiration dates at the end of 2027 and incur no recurring funding fees. OKX also offers contracts with no expiration dates, but uses a different funding mechanism.

The investment is a bet that financial markets have yet to catch up with the enormous amounts of money flowing into artificial intelligence, according to Village Global.

"AI is driving one of the largest investment cycles in history, despite the financial infrastructure around it remaining quite underdeveloped," said Max Killberg of Village Global. He said the firm sees an opportunity to develop financial markets around AI, rather than simply back another prediction market.

Manifold Markets co-founder Stephen Gruggett told CoinDesk that MNX’s approach is better suited to private companies such as OpenAI and Anthropic, whose shares trade infrequently and are difficult to price.

"OpenAI, Anthropic secondaries are illiquid and hard to price," he said. "A perp based on an illiquid, stale price is worse than meaningless: it doesn't behave the way investors expect; it's easy to manipulate; and it may have a very high and unpredictable funding rate."

Traders can also use up to three times their available funds, increasing both potential profits and losses.

Prices are determined by trading activity on MNX rather than an external price feed. If a company remains private when its contract expires, the exchange uses publicly available valuations from funding rounds, investment funds or secondary markets. As a last resort, MNX can determine the settlement price itself, subject to a published review princess.

That means traders could end up settling their bets at a price different from what investors might actually pay for shares in a private transaction.

The exchange does not currently serve U.S. customers, although Grugett said it plans to obtain the necessary licenses.

MNX also aims to offer markets around the wider AI economy, including company revenue, employment, housing, the AI supply chain and computing capacity.

AI has become a huge sponge for investment capital, although exposure to the boom is concentrated in a handful of tech companies. The largest U.S. hyperscalers are expected to spend at least $800 billion this year and more than $1 trillion the next, Bitcoin Suisse’s Crypto Wealth Management Report 2026 shows.

If a company remains private when its contract expires, the exchange uses publicly available valuations from funding rounds, investment funds or secondary markets. As a last resort, MNX can determine the settlement price itself, subject to a published review princess.

That means traders could end up settling their bets at a price different from what investors might actually pay for shares in a private transaction.

The exchange does not currently serve U.S. customers, although Grugett said it plans to obtain the necessary licenses.

MNX also aims to offer markets around the wider AI economy, including company revenue, employment, housing, the AI supply chain and computing capacity.

AI has become a huge sponge for investment capital, although exposure to the boom is concentrated in a handful of tech companies. The largest U.S. hyperscalers are expected to spend at least $800 billion this year and more than $1 trillion the next, Bitcoin Suisse’s Crypto Wealth Management Report 2026 shows.
